```{r}
plot(NA, xlim = range(yrs) + c(-0.5, 0.5), ylim = c(0.5, nrow(st) + 0.5),
     xlab = "Season", ylab = "", yaxt = "n", xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
axis(2, at = seq_len(nrow(st)),
     labels = sprintf("%s, %d m", st$station, round(st$elevation_m)),
     las = 1, tick = FALSE)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(st))) for (y in yrs) {
  r <- cv[cv$station == st$station[i] & cv$year == y, ]
  if (!nrow(r) || r$status == "station not reporting") next
  rect(y - 0.5, i - 0.5, y + 0.5, i + 0.5,
       col = ramp[1 + round(100 * r$observed_fraction)], border = NA)
  if (r$status == "kept")
    rect(y - 0.5, i - 0.5, y + 0.5, i + 0.5, border = "grey20", lwd = 0.7)
  else points(y, i, pch = 4, cex = 0.55, col = "#943126")
}
par(xpd = NA)
legend(min(yrs) - 0.5, -0.35, horiz = TRUE, bty = "n", cex = 0.75,
       legend = c("kept, 95 per cent or more observed", "dropped for coverage",
                  "shading, share of hours observed, 0 (pale) to 1 (dark)"),
       pch = c(0, 4, 15), col = c("grey20", "#943126", "#1B4F72"),
       pt.cex = c(1.2, 0.7, 1.2))
par(op)
```

@fig-coverage shows what the table cannot, which is when each station reported. The network was switched on and off for operational reasons, so `r n_dropped_pre2000` of the `r n_dropped` dropped seasons fell before 2000, and the `r station_prose(late_station)` station reported only from `r max(first_report)`.

### Season Window

The window was a fixed calendar one, 1 May to 30 September, 153 days, with the calculation spun up from 1 April so that thirty days of weather preceded the first reported day.

That was a departure from the original design, which proposed the Canadian rule that section C-2.3 of @cffdg2025fwi2025 describes as the criterion most often used across Canada, to "start calculation three days after the disappearance of snow cover", or, where snow cover cannot be observed, after three days above 12 degrees Celsius [@lawson2008weather]. The rule was implemented, run, and abandoned, because these stations do not report through the winter, so the rule fired on whatever day a station was switched on, and the station reporting record above shows that the switch-on date varied by station and season for operational reasons. The same constraint has been met before. @field2015gfwed, building the Global Fire Weather Database, noted that data for their Canadian comparison stations "were available only for the fire season, which was determined using a temperature threshold" [@field2015gfwed, p. 1411], and @hanes2020overwinter, working with fire weather stations in Alberta and Ontario, took winter precipitation from nearby Environment and Climate Change Canada stations because "fire weather stations are not operated during the winter" [@hanes2020overwinter, p. 5].

One consequence was stated rather than repaired. Fire season length could not be estimated from this network and was therefore not among the metrics, although lengthening season is among the most-reported fire danger trends, because a network whose stations are switched on and off for operational reasons cannot measure when a season begins. The published definitions of the season answer different questions and fail in different ways on a record like this one. The weather rule of @lawson2008weather and @wotton1993seasonlength, which @mcelhinny2020era5 stated as a season "active on the fourth day following 3 consecutive days with a maximum temperature of 12 °C or higher" and over "after 3 consecutive days with a maximum temperature of 5 °C or lower" [@mcelhinny2020era5, p. 1826], dates the weather season and needs a record that runs through the shoulder months. @jolly2015global defined fire weather season length from the danger series itself, as "the number of days each year when fire danger is above half its value range" [@jolly2015global, p. 2], and found that it lengthened across 25.3 per cent of the Earth's vegetated surface from 1979 to 2013, a definition that dates the danger season and needs the stations to be reporting before the first such day. Definitions based on fires rather than weather date the fire season: @westerling2016increasing measured it from the first discovery to the last control of a large fire and found western United States forest fire seasons in 2003 to 2012 more than 84 days longer than in 1973 to 1982, @albertgreen2013timing dated its start and end where a smoothed daily lightning-fire risk curve crossed set thresholds in Alberta and Ontario, and @granville2026season dated it from observed wildfires across Ontario and found it lengthening by a median of about 0.5 days per year in the northwest. Those need a complete and well-dated ignition record, which @sec-data shows the basin's record is not after 2000. The metrics that remained here were counts and sums over a window of fixed length, which the network can measure, and what that window gives up is taken up in @sec-discussion.

### Data Limitation: Gaps and Startup

Runs of missing temperature, humidity or wind up to 24 hours were filled by linear interpolation, since the reference implementation requires a gap-free hourly stream, and missing precipitation was filled with zero, because rain cannot be invented. A station-season was kept only where at least 95 per cent of the 1 April to 30 September hours were observed and no single gap exceeded 24 hours.

Filling a gap with no rain makes a missing wet spell look dry and pushes danger up. The direction matters and is stated. Coverage in this record was worse early than late, so this bias, where it acted, inflated danger in early seasons and therefore worked against an increasing trend rather than for one. It was identical across the three series by construction, since all three ran on the same filled record, and so could not move a contrast between versions.

Each station-season started from FFMC 85, DMC 6 and DC 15, the values @vanwagner1987fwi gives and the reference implementation defaults to. The Drought Code was not overwintered, because these stations report no winter weather for an overwintering calculation to run on. That departs from provincial practice, since @hanes2020overwinter reported that "the western provinces regularly overwinter the DC" [@hanes2020overwinter, p. 2], adjusting the fall value by the precipitation received over winter. The departure matters for absolute counts. @mcelhinny2020era5 computed a global Fire Weather Index reanalysis for 1979 to 2018 both ways and found that "even a modest difference in FWI values at start-up can lead to important differences in the number and spatial distribution of fire spread days between the overwintered and default calculations" [@mcelhinny2020era5, p. 1829], illustrated with the 2016 season over North America, when fuel moisture before the Fort McMurray fire in Alberta followed low overwinter precipitation and severe fall drought. The Drought Code here therefore carried startup information into early May in every season, identically in all three series, and its effect on absolute Drought Code, Buildup Index and extreme-day levels is reported with the implementation checks in @sec-results.

## Fire Activity

```{r}
#| label: ignition-inputs
#| echo: false
#| output: false
ign_daily <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "ignitions-daily.csv"), stringsAsFactors = F)
ign_daily$date <- as.Date(ign_daily$date)
completeness <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "ignition-completeness.csv"),stringsAsFactors = F)
attribution <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "ignition-attribution.csv"), stringsAsFactors = F)

n_total_incidents <- sum(completeness$n_incidents)
n_dated <- sum(completeness$n_dated)
n_undated <- n_total_incidents - n_dated
pct_dated <- round(100 * n_dated / n_total_incidents, 1)

# Dating completeness by decade, computed here so the sentence below quotes the
# table rather than describing it from memory.
completeness$decade <- paste0(completeness$year %/% 10 * 10, "s")
cd_pre <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(completeness, completeness$decade), function(d)
  data.frame(decade = d$decade[1],
             pct_dated = 100 * sum(d$n_dated) / sum(d$n_incidents))))
cd_pre <- cd_pre[order(cd_pre$decade), ]
```

The ignition record was the BC Wildfire Service historical incident set [@bcws2026incidents], clipped to the basin, `r n_fmt(n_total_incidents)` incidents over the `r sa("first_year")` to `r sa("last_year")` seasons.

Two properties of that record governed what could be asked of it, and neither was repaired here, because neither can be. First, many incidents could not be placed on a day at all. `r n_fmt(n_dated)` of `r n_fmt(n_total_incidents)` incidents, `r pct_dated` per cent, carried an ignition date, and the remaining `r n_fmt(n_undated)` could not enter a daily series at any threshold. The missing dates were not spread evenly, and they did not concentrate where intuition puts them, in that the earliest decade in the record was `r round(head(cd_pre$pct_dated, 1), 0)` per cent dated and the most recent was `r round(tail(cd_pre$pct_dated, 1), 0)` per cent. Missing date and missing cause were largely the same records. Second, cause attribution was not stationary. @tbl-completeness gives both by decade, and a lightning-caused count that falls after 2000 may record a change in how cause was coded rather than a change in ignition.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-completeness
#| tbl-cap: "Completeness of the ignition record by decade. A dated incident can be placed on a day; an attributed incident carries a recorded cause. Both fall sharply after 2000 and the same records are usually missing both."
#| echo: true
completeness$decade <- paste0(completeness$year %/% 10 * 10, "s")
cd <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(completeness, completeness$decade), function(d) {
  data.frame(
    Decade = d$decade[1],
    Incidents = sum(d$n_incidents),
    Dated = sum(d$n_dated),
    `Dated %` = round(100 * sum(d$n_dated) / sum(d$n_incidents), 1),
    Attributed = sum(d$n_caused),
    `Attributed %` = round(100 * sum(d$n_caused) / sum(d$n_incidents), 1),
    check.names = FALSE)
}))
fmt_tbl(cd)
```

```{r}
#| label: ignition-caption
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Season-by-cause counts and the two completeness measures, with the pooled
# shares before 2000 and from 2000 onward computed here for the caption.
ibs <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "ignitions-by-season.csv"),
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cause_tab <- xtabs(n ~ fire_cause + fire_year, ibs)
cause_tab <- cause_tab[c("Lightning", "Person", "Unknown"), , drop = FALSE]
share <- function(rows, col) 100 * sum(completeness[[col]][rows]) / sum(completeness$n_incidents[rows])
ign_cap <- sprintf(paste(
  "Ignitions by season and the completeness of their records. Upper panel,",
  "incidents per season by reported cause, %s in all. Lower panel, the share",
  "of incidents carrying an ignition date and the share carrying a recorded",
  "cause, which were %.0f and %.0f per cent before 2000 and %.0f and %.0f per",
  "cent from 2000 onward. Both panels are the same records, so the fall in the",
  "lower panel is what makes the cause split in the upper panel unreadable as",
  "an ignition trend after 2000."),
  n_fmt(n_total_incidents),
  share(completeness$year < 2000, "n_dated"), share(completeness$year < 2000, "n_caused"),
  share(completeness$year >= 2000, "n_dated"), share(completeness$year >= 2000, "n_caused"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ignitions
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-dpi: 300
#| fig-cap: !expr ign_cap
# Two panels on one season axis. The bars are stacked by cause in the palette
# the study-area map uses; the lines are the two completeness measures from the
# same completeness table the decade table summarises.
cause_cols <- c(Lightning = "#1B7A5A", Person = "#B3242B", Unknown = "grey60")
yrs2 <- as.integer(colnames(cause_tab))
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(1.2, 4.2, 0.6, 1), oma = c(2.5, 0, 0, 0),
          mgp = c(2.4, 0.7, 0), cex = 0.75)
barplot(cause_tab, col = cause_cols[rownames(cause_tab)], border = NA,
        names.arg = rep("", ncol(cause_tab)), ylab = "Ignitions per season",
        space = 0, xaxs = "i")
legend("topright", legend = rownames(cause_tab), fill = cause_cols[rownames(cause_tab)],
       border = NA, bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
par(mar = c(3.2, 4.2, 0.6, 1))
plot(completeness$year, completeness$pct_dated, type = "l", lwd = 1.8,
     col = "#1B4F72", ylim = c(0, 100), xlab = "Season",
     ylab = "Per cent of incidents", xaxs = "i", xlim = range(yrs2) + c(-0.5, 0.5))
lines(completeness$year, completeness$pct_caused, lwd = 1.8, col = "#B7950B", lty = 2)
legend("bottomleft", legend = c("dated", "cause attributed"),
       col = c("#1B4F72", "#B7950B"), lwd = 1.8, lty = c(1, 2), bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
par(op)
```

@fig-ignitions shows the same records season by season. The upper panel gives the counts by cause and the lower panel the two completeness measures, and the fall in the lower panel after 2000 is what makes the cause split in the upper panel unreadable as an ignition trend.

The design responded to both rather than caveating them. The ignition models below carry season as a fixed effect, so the danger coefficient is identified only from day-to-day variation inside a season. Reporting completeness and cause coding both change between seasons and neither changes within one, so a between-season contrast would confound the danger effect with the record keeping and a within-season contrast cannot. Three response series were modelled, lightning, person-caused and all causes together, because the all-cause series cannot be affected by cause coding at all and is therefore the one that decides when the three disagree. Because detection of small fires also improved over the record, every result was reported at three minimum sizes, no limit, one hectare and four hectares, and a conclusion that survived at only one threshold was reported as not surviving.

# Methods {#sec-methods}

```{r}
#| label: review-terms
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Search terms come only from the manuscript's own title and keywords, so a reader
# can trace every term to the front matter. Candidates are written once; the
# selection is typed into the file and never overwritten by a render.
if (!file.exists("../04.references/review/search-terms.csv")) {
  front <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(knitr::current_input())
  small <- c("a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "by", "do", "does", "for", "from", "how", "in", "into", "is", "its", "of", "on", "or", "the", "to", "under", "using", "versus", "what", "why", "with")
  phrases <- \(x) x |>
    stringr::str_to_lower() |>
    stringr::str_remove_all("[*_]") |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("[^[:alnum:][:space:]-]", " | ") |>
    stringr::str_replace_all(paste0("\\b(", paste(small, collapse = "|"), ")\\b"), " | ") |>
    stringr::str_split_1("\\|") |>
    stringr::str_squish() |>
    purrr::keep(\(p) nchar(p) > 2)
  dir.create("../04.references/review", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(term = stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_to_lower(unlist(stringr::str_split(unlist(front$keywords), "[;,]")))), source = "keywords"),
    tibble::tibble(term = phrases(front$title), source = "title"),
    tibble::tibble(term = phrases(front$subtitle %||% ""), source = "subtitle")
  ) |>
    dplyr::distinct(term, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::mutate(question = NA, concept = NA) |>
    readr::write_csv("../04.references/review/search-terms.csv", na = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-queries
#| echo: true
#| output: false
front <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(knitr::current_input())
declared <- paste(front$title, front$subtitle, paste(unlist(front$keywords), collapse = " ")) |>
  stringr::str_remove_all("[*_]") |>
  stringr::str_to_lower()
term_regex <- \(x) if (stringr::str_ends(x, "\\*")) paste0("\\b", stringr::str_escape(stringr::str_remove(x, "\\*$"))) else paste0("\\b", stringr::str_escape(x), "\\b")
terms <- readr::read_csv("../04.references/review/search-terms.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(question), !is.na(concept)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(term = stringr::str_to_lower(term)) |>
  tidyr::separate_longer_delim(question, " ")
stray <- terms$term[!purrr::map_lgl(terms$term, \(x) stringr::str_detect(declared, term_regex(x)))]
if (nrow(terms) == 0) stop("No search terms selected in 04.references/review/search-terms.csv")
if (length(stray) > 0) stop("Not in the title, subtitle or keywords: ", paste(unique(stray), collapse = ", "))
queries <- terms |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = c(question, concept), group = paste(term, collapse = "|")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = question, route = paste(c(dplyr::first(question), concept), collapse = "-"), concepts = paste(group, collapse = " AND "))
# One boolean string per query for the external indexes. A term ending in * is a
# stem; the external indexes stem on their own, so the star is dropped there.
boolean_query <- function(concepts, or = " OR ", and = " AND ") {
  stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND ") |>
    purrr::map_chr(\(g) paste0("(", paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(g, "\\|"), \(x) {
      x <- stringr::str_remove(x, "\\*$")
      if (grepl(" ", x)) paste0('"', x, '"') else x
    }), collapse = or), ")")) |>
    paste(collapse = and)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-store
#| echo: true
#| output: false
if (!file.exists("../02.inputs/derived/review-store-hits.csv")) {
  # library-science manifest, https://github.com/seamusrobertmurphy/library-science/blob/main/library/manifest.csv
  manifest <- readr::read_csv("../../library-science/library/manifest.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
  # library-science source notes, https://github.com/seamusrobertmurphy/library-science/tree/main/sources
  notes <- tibble::tibble(path = list.files("../../library-science/sources", "\\.md$", full.names = TRUE)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(key = tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(path)), note = purrr::map_chr(path, \(p) paste(readLines(p, warn = FALSE), collapse = " ")))
  store <- manifest |>
    dplyr::filter(status %in% c("verified", "filed", "unverified"), !is.na(title) | !is.na(key)) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(notes, key, note), by = "key") |>
    dplyr::mutate(text = stringr::str_to_lower(paste(title, note)))
  hits <- queries |>
    purrr::pmap(\(question, route, concepts) {
      groups <- stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND ")
      term <- \(x) if (stringr::str_ends(x, "\\*")) paste0(stringr::str_remove(x, "\\*$"), "\\w*") else paste0(x, "\\b")
      patterns <- purrr::map_chr(groups, \(g) paste0("\\b(", paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(g, "\\|"), term), collapse = "|"), ")"))
      keep <- purrr::map(patterns, \(r) stringr::str_detect(store$text, r)) |> purrr::reduce(`&`)
      store[keep, ] |> dplyr::transmute(question, route = paste0("store-", route), key, doi, title, year, venue = container, source_note = dplyr::if_else(has_source_note == "yes", key, NA))
    }) |>
    purrr::list_rbind()
  readr::write_csv(hits, "../02.inputs/derived/review-store-hits.csv")
  queries |>
    dplyr::transmute(strand = "library-science", route = paste0("store-", route), query = concepts, date = as.character(Sys.Date())) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::count(hits, route, name = "retrieved"), by = "route") |>
    dplyr::mutate(retrieved = tidyr::replace_na(retrieved, 0L), reported_total = retrieved, cap = NA, capped = FALSE, error = NA) |>
    readr::write_csv("../02.inputs/derived/review-search-log.csv")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-openalex
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# OpenAlex searches titles and abstracts. Abstracts are publisher text and are
# written only under 02.inputs/searches, which is not committed; the committed
# hits file carries bibliographic fields alone.
if (!file.exists("../02.inputs/derived/review-openalex-hits.csv")) {
  abstract_text <- function(inv) {
    if (is.null(inv)) return(NA_character_)
    pos <- unlist(inv, use.names = FALSE)
    words <- rep(names(inv), lengths(inv))
    paste(words[order(pos)], collapse = " ")
  }
  search_oa <- function(question, route, concepts, cap = 3000) {
    query <- boolean_query(concepts)
    works <- list(); cursor <- "*"; total <- NA; err <- NA
    repeat {
      # OpenAlex works endpoint, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/search-works
      resp <- httr2::request("https://api.openalex.org/works") |>
        httr2::req_url_query(filter = paste0("title_and_abstract.search:", query, ",from_publication_date:1987-01-01"),
                             select = "id,doi,title,publication_year,primary_location,type,cited_by_count,abstract_inverted_index",
                             `per-page` = 200, cursor = cursor, mailto = "seamusrobertmurphy@gmail.com") |>
        httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 6) |>
        httr2::req_error(is_error = \(r) FALSE) |>
        httr2::req_perform()
      if (httr2::resp_status(resp) != 200) { err <- paste("HTTP", httr2::resp_status(resp)); break }
      body <- httr2::resp_body_json(resp)
      total <- body$meta$count; cursor <- body$meta$next_cursor
      works <- c(works, body$results)
      if (is.null(cursor) || length(body$results) == 0 || length(works) >= cap) break
    }
    rows <- works |>
      purrr::map(\(w) tibble::tibble(
        openalex = w$id %||% NA_character_,
        doi = stringr::str_remove(w$doi %||% NA_character_, "^https://doi.org/"),
        title = w$title %||% NA_character_, year = w$publication_year %||% NA_integer_,
        venue = w$primary_location$source$display_name %||% NA_character_,
        type = w$type %||% NA_character_, citations = w$cited_by_count %||% NA_integer_,
        abstract = abstract_text(w$abstract_inverted_index))) |>
      purrr::list_rbind()
    list(hits = dplyr::mutate(rows, question, route = paste0("openalex-", route), .before = 1),
         log = tibble::tibble(strand = "openalex", route = paste0("openalex-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()),
                              retrieved = nrow(rows), reported_total = total, cap, capped = isTRUE(total > cap), error = err))
  }
  runs <- purrr::pmap(queries, search_oa)
  oa <- purrr::map(runs, "hits") |> purrr::list_rbind()
  dir.create("../02.inputs/searches", showWarnings = FALSE)
  readr::write_csv(oa, "../02.inputs/searches/review-openalex-records.csv")
  readr::write_csv(dplyr::select(oa, -abstract), "../02.inputs/derived/review-openalex-hits.csv")
  readr::read_csv("../02.inputs/derived/review-search-log.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows(purrr::map(runs, "log") |> purrr::list_rbind() |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), as.character))) |>
    readr::write_csv("../02.inputs/derived/review-search-log.csv")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-ads
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# NASA ADS searches abstracts with a personal token read from outside the
# repository. The token "trend" is a stopword in ADS, so any query carrying it
# is run without that concept and logged as such.
if (!file.exists("../02.inputs/derived/review-ads-hits.csv")) {
  token_file <- path.expand("~/.ads/dev_key")
  search_ads <- function(question, route, concepts, cap = 2000) {
    groups <- stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND ")
    dropped <- groups[stringr::str_detect(groups, "^trend")]
    groups <- groups[!stringr::str_detect(groups, "^trend")]
    query <- paste0("abs:", boolean_query(paste(groups, collapse = " AND ")), " year:1987-")
    rows <- tibble::tibble(); total <- NA; err <- NA; start <- 0
    if (!file.exists(token_file)) err <- "no token" else repeat {
      # NASA ADS search API, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/help/api/api-docs.html
      resp <- httr2::request("https://api.adsabs.harvard.edu/v1/search/query") |>
        httr2::req_headers(Authorization = paste("Bearer", readLines(token_file, warn = FALSE)[1])) |>
        httr2::req_url_query(q = query, fl = "bibcode,title,year,pub,doi,doctype,abstract", rows = 200, start = start) |>
        httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 4) |>
        httr2::req_error(is_error = \(r) FALSE) |>
        httr2::req_perform()
      if (httr2::resp_status(resp) != 200) { err <- paste("HTTP", httr2::resp_status(resp)); break }
      body <- httr2::resp_body_json(resp)$response
      total <- body$numFound
      page <- body$docs |>
        purrr::map(\(d) tibble::tibble(bibcode = d$bibcode %||% NA_character_, doi = unlist(d$doi)[1] %||% NA_character_,
                                       title = unlist(d$title)[1] %||% NA_character_, year = as.integer(d$year %||% NA),
                                       venue = d$pub %||% NA_character_, type = d$doctype %||% NA_character_,
                                       abstract = d$abstract %||% NA_character_)) |>
        purrr::list_rbind()
      rows <- dplyr::bind_rows(rows, page)
      start <- start + 200
      if (nrow(page) == 0 || start >= total || nrow(rows) >= cap) break
    }
    list(hits = dplyr::mutate(rows, question, route = paste0("ads-", route), .before = 1),
         log = tibble::tibble(strand = "ads", route = paste0("ads-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()),
                              retrieved = nrow(rows), reported_total = total, cap, capped = isTRUE(total > cap),
                              error = dplyr::coalesce(err, if (length(dropped)) paste("stopword concept dropped:", dropped) else NA)))
  }
  runs <- purrr::pmap(queries, search_ads)
  ads <- purrr::map(runs, "hits") |> purrr::list_rbind()
  readr::write_csv(ads, "../02.inputs/searches/review-ads-records.csv")
  readr::write_csv(dplyr::select(ads, -abstract), "../02.inputs/derived/review-ads-hits.csv")
  readr::read_csv("../02.inputs/derived/review-search-log.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows(purrr::map(runs, "log") |> purrr::list_rbind() |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), as.character))) |>
    readr::write_csv("../02.inputs/derived/review-search-log.csv")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-semantic-scholar
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Semantic Scholar is the index the library protocol names. Without a key it
# rate limits, so a refusal is logged against the query rather than stopping
# the render, and the log row says which strand is missing.
if (!file.exists("../02.inputs/derived/review-s2-hits.csv")) {
  search_s2 <- function(question, route, concepts, cap = 3000) {
    query <- boolean_query(concepts, or = " | ", and = " + ")
    papers <- list(); token <- NULL; total <- NA; err <- NA
    repeat {
      # Semantic Scholar Academic Graph bulk search, https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/graph#tag/Paper-Data/operation/get_graph_paper_bulk_search
      resp <- httr2::request("https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search/bulk") |>
        httr2::req_url_query(query = query, year = "1987-", fields = "title,year,venue,externalIds,citationCount,publicationTypes", token = token) |>
        httr2::req_throttle(rate = 1 / 2) |>
        httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 3, backoff = \(i) 5 * i) |>
        httr2::req_error(is_error = \(r) FALSE) |>
        httr2::req_perform()
      if (httr2::resp_status(resp) != 200) { err <- paste("HTTP", httr2::resp_status(resp)); break }
      body <- httr2::resp_body_json(resp)
      total <- body$total; token <- body$token
      papers <- c(papers, body$data)
      if (is.null(token) || length(papers) >= cap) break
    }
    works <- papers |>
      purrr::map(\(w) tibble::tibble(doi = w$externalIds$DOI %||% NA_character_, title = w$title %||% NA_character_, year = w$year %||% NA_integer_, venue = w$venue %||% NA_character_, type = paste(unlist(w$publicationTypes), collapse = " "), citations = w$citationCount %||% NA_integer_)) |>
      purrr::list_rbind()
    list(hits = dplyr::mutate(works, question, route = paste0("s2-", route), .before = 1),
         log = tibble::tibble(strand = "semantic-scholar", route = paste0("s2-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()), retrieved = nrow(works), reported_total = total, cap, capped = isTRUE(total > cap), error = err))
  }
  runs <- purrr::pmap(queries, search_s2)
  readr::write_csv(purrr::map(runs, "hits") |> purrr::list_rbind(), "../02.inputs/derived/review-s2-hits.csv")
  readr::read_csv("../02.inputs/derived/review-search-log.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows(purrr::map(runs, "log") |> purrr::list_rbind() |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), as.character))) |>
    readr::write_csv("../02.inputs/derived/review-search-log.csv")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-chase
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# One round of backward and forward chasing from the central records, through
# OpenAlex, which lists both the references of a work and the works citing it.
central <- c("10.4095/st000101", "10.1175/waf-d-23-0226.1", "10.1016/j.agrformet.2018.07.005",
             "10.1007/s10584-012-0667-2", "10.1071/wf17008", "10.1071/wf11088")
if (length(central) > 0 && !file.exists("../02.inputs/derived/review-chase-hits.csv")) {
  oa_get <- function(url, query = list()) {
    resp <- httr2::request(url) |> httr2::req_url_query(!!!query, mailto = "seamusrobertmurphy@gmail.com") |>
      httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 6) |> httr2::req_error(is_error = \(r) FALSE) |> httr2::req_perform()
    if (httr2::resp_status(resp) != 200) return(NULL)
    httr2::resp_body_json(resp)
  }
  as_row <- \(w) tibble::tibble(openalex = w$id %||% NA_character_, doi = stringr::str_remove(w$doi %||% NA_character_, "^https://doi.org/"), title = w$title %||% NA_character_, year = w$publication_year %||% NA_integer_, venue = w$primary_location$source$display_name %||% NA_character_)
  chase <- function(seed_doi) {
    # OpenAlex works endpoint, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works
    seed <- oa_get(paste0("https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/", seed_doi))
    if (is.null(seed)) return(tibble::tibble(seed = seed_doi, route = "chase", error = "seed not found"))
    refs <- if (length(seed$referenced_works)) oa_get("https://api.openalex.org/works", list(filter = paste0("ids.openalex:", paste(basename(unlist(seed$referenced_works)), collapse = "|")), `per-page` = 200, select = "id,doi,title,publication_year,primary_location")) else NULL
    cites <- oa_get("https://api.openalex.org/works", list(filter = paste0("cites:", basename(seed$id)), `per-page` = 200, select = "id,doi,title,publication_year,primary_location"))
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      purrr::map(refs$results %||% list(), as_row) |> purrr::list_rbind() |> dplyr::mutate(route = "chase-references"),
      purrr::map(cites$results %||% list(), as_row) |> purrr::list_rbind() |> dplyr::mutate(route = "chase-citations")
    ) |> dplyr::mutate(seed = seed_doi, .before = 1)
  }
  chased <- purrr::map(central, chase) |> purrr::list_rbind()
  readr::write_csv(chased, "../02.inputs/derived/review-chase-hits.csv")
  readr::read_csv("../02.inputs/derived/review-search-log.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows(chased |> dplyr::count(seed, route, name = "retrieved") |>
      dplyr::transmute(strand = "openalex-chase", route = paste(route, seed), query = seed, date = as.character(Sys.Date()),
                       retrieved = as.character(retrieved), reported_total = retrieved, cap = NA, capped = "FALSE", error = NA)) |>
    readr::write_csv("../02.inputs/derived/review-search-log.csv")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-records
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# One row per unique record across every strand. A record already cited by this
# manuscript is marked, by DOI against the bibliography, so screening can see
# what the earlier reading had reached.
if (!file.exists("../02.inputs/derived/review-records.csv")) {
  read_hits <- \(p) if (file.exists(p)) readr::read_csv(p, col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) else tibble::tibble()
  bib <- paste(readLines("../04.references/references.bib", warn = FALSE), collapse = " ")
  bib_dois <- stringr::str_to_lower(unlist(stringr::str_extract_all(bib, "10\\.[0-9]{4,9}/[^\\s,}\"]+")))
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    read_hits("../02.inputs/derived/review-store-hits.csv"),
    read_hits("../02.inputs/derived/review-openalex-hits.csv"),
    read_hits("../02.inputs/derived/review-ads-hits.csv"),
    read_hits("../02.inputs/derived/review-s2-hits.csv"),
    read_hits("../02.inputs/derived/review-chase-hits.csv") |> dplyr::mutate(question = "chase")
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(doi = stringr::str_to_lower(doi),
                  id = dplyr::coalesce(doi, stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_to_lower(stringr::str_replace_all(title, "[^[:alnum:] ]", " "))))) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(id), id != "") |>
    dplyr::summarise(.by = id, doi = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(doi)), title = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(title)), year = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(year)), venue = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(venue)), type = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(type)), questions = paste(sort(unique(question)), collapse = " "), routes = paste(sort(unique(route)), collapse = " "), duplicates_merged = dplyr::n(), key = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(key)), source_note = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(source_note))) |>
    dplyr::mutate(cited = dplyr::if_else(!is.na(doi) & doi %in% bib_dois, "yes", "no"), decision = NA, reason = NA, full_text = NA) |>
    readr::write_csv("../02.inputs/derived/review-records.csv", na = "")
}
```

```{python}
#| label: review-screening-pack
#| echo: true
#| output: false
"""Build the title-and-abstract screening batches for the 2026-10-13 literature review.

Reads the committed screening table 02.inputs/derived/review-records.csv, applies the
document-type rule of the review protocol (records of an ineligible type are excluded by
rule with the code not-research), attaches each remaining record's abstract from the
uncommitted search files under 02.inputs/searches, fetches the abstract from OpenAlex by
DOI where no search file holds it, and writes one batch per question under
02.inputs/searches/review-batches/. Abstracts are publisher text and never leave
02.inputs/searches. Runs only while no batch folder exists.
"""
import csv, json, os, sys, time, urllib.parse, urllib.request

ROOT = os.path.abspath("..")
DERIVED = os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "derived")
SEARCHES = os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "searches")
BATCHES = os.path.join(SEARCHES, "review-batches")
MAILTO = "seamusrobertmurphy@gmail.com"
INELIGIBLE = {"abstract", "conference-abstract", "dataset", "peer-review", "paratext", "erratum", "editorial", "letter", "other"}

def read(p):
    with open(p, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader(f))

def write(p, rows, fields):
    with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fields); w.writeheader(); w.writerows(rows)

def abstract_from_inverted(inv):
    if not inv: return ""
    pos = []
    for word, idx in inv.items():
        for i in idx: pos.append((i, word))
    return " ".join(w for _, w in sorted(pos))

def fetch_openalex(dois):
    out = {}
    for i in range(0, len(dois), 50):
        chunk = dois[i:i + 50]
        # OpenAlex works endpoint, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works
        url = "https://api.openalex.org/works?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({
            "filter": "doi:" + "|".join(chunk), "per-page": 50,
            "select": "doi,abstract_inverted_index,type", "mailto": MAILTO})
        for attempt in range(4):
            try:
                with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as r:
                    body = json.load(r)
                break
            except Exception as e:
                time.sleep(3 * (attempt + 1)); body = {"results": []}
        for w in body.get("results", []):
            d = (w.get("doi") or "").replace("https://doi.org/", "").lower()
            out[d] = (abstract_from_inverted(w.get("abstract_inverted_index")), w.get("type") or "")
        time.sleep(0.2)
    return out

def main():
    records = read(os.path.join(DERIVED, "review-records.csv"))
    abstracts = {}
    for name in ("review-openalex-records.csv", "review-ads-records.csv"):
        p = os.path.join(SEARCHES, name)
        if not os.path.exists(p): continue
        for r in read(p):
            key = (r.get("doi") or "").lower() or r["title"].lower()
            if r.get("abstract"): abstracts.setdefault(key, r["abstract"])
    need = [r["doi"] for r in records if r["doi"] and r["doi"].lower() not in abstracts]
    fetched = fetch_openalex(need)
    for d, (a, t) in fetched.items():
        if a: abstracts[d] = a
    n_rule = 0
    for r in records:
        if not r["type"] and r["doi"] and r["doi"].lower() in fetched:
            r["type"] = fetched[r["doi"].lower()][1]
        if r["type"] in INELIGIBLE:
            r["decision"], r["reason"] = "exclude", "not-research"; n_rule += 1
    write(os.path.join(DERIVED, "review-records.csv"), records, list(records[0].keys()))
    os.makedirs(BATCHES, exist_ok=True)
    batches = {}
    for r in records:
        if r["decision"]: continue
        key = (r["doi"] or "").lower() or r["id"]
        row = {"id": r["id"], "doi": r["doi"], "title": r["title"], "year": r["year"], "venue": r["venue"],
               "type": r["type"], "questions": r["questions"], "cited": r["cited"],
               "abstract": abstracts.get(key, "")}
        q = r["questions"].split()[0] if r["questions"] else "chase"
        batches.setdefault(q, []).append(row)
    fields = ["id", "doi", "title", "year", "venue", "type", "questions", "cited", "abstract"]
    for q, rows in batches.items():
        if q == "chase" and len(rows) > 220:
            half = (len(rows) + 1) // 2
            write(os.path.join(BATCHES, "chase-a.csv"), rows[:half], fields)
            write(os.path.join(BATCHES, "chase-b.csv"), rows[half:], fields)
        else:
            write(os.path.join(BATCHES, f"{q}.csv"), rows, fields)
    print("records", len(records), "excluded by type rule", n_rule,
          "to screen", sum(len(v) for v in batches.values()),
          "with abstract", sum(1 for v in batches.values() for r in v if r["abstract"]))
    for q, rows in batches.items(): print(" ", q, len(rows))

if not os.path.isdir(BATCHES):
    main()
```

```{python}
#| label: review-screening-merge
#| echo: true
#| output: false
"""Merge the screening decisions of the 2026-10-13 literature review into the screening table.

Reads every decisions-*.csv under 02.inputs/searches/review-batches/, checks that each id
was decided exactly once and that every exclusion carries a code from the protocol, and
writes decision, reason and note into 02.inputs/derived/review-records.csv. A record that
already carries a decision in the table (hand-found records, records excluded by the
document-type rule) keeps it. Runs only while a row of the table has no decision.
"""
import csv, glob, os, sys

ROOT = os.path.abspath("..")
TABLE = os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "derived", "review-records.csv")
BATCHES = os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "searches", "review-batches")
CODES = {"off-topic", "wrong-population", "wrong-concept", "not-research", "out-of-window", "not-english", "duplicate"}

def main():
    with open(TABLE, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
    fields = list(rows[0].keys())
    if "note" not in fields: fields.append("note")
    decided = {}
    for p in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(BATCHES, "decisions-*.csv"))):
        with open(p, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
            for d in csv.DictReader(f):
                if d["id"] in decided:
                    sys.exit(f"id decided twice: {d['id']} in {p}")
                if d["decision"] not in {"include", "exclude", "undecided"}:
                    sys.exit(f"bad decision {d['decision']!r} for {d['id']} in {p}")
                if d["decision"] == "exclude" and d["reason"] not in CODES:
                    sys.exit(f"bad reason {d['reason']!r} for {d['id']} in {p}")
                decided[d["id"]] = d
    n_set = 0
    for r in rows:
        r.setdefault("note", "")
        if r.get("decision"):
            continue
        d = decided.get(r["id"])
        if d:
            r["decision"], r["reason"], r["note"] = d["decision"], d["reason"], d.get("note", ""); n_set += 1
    missing = [r["id"] for r in rows if not r.get("decision")]
    with open(TABLE, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fields); w.writeheader(); w.writerows(rows)
    from collections import Counter
    print("decisions merged", n_set, "| undecided rows left without any decision", len(missing))
    print("by decision", Counter(r["decision"] for r in rows).most_common())
    print("by reason", Counter(r["reason"] for r in rows if r["decision"] == "exclude").most_common())
    if missing: print("first missing ids", missing[:10])

with open(TABLE, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
    undecided_rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(f) if not r.get("decision")]
if undecided_rows:
    main()
```

```{python}
#| label: review-fulltext-fetch
#| echo: true
#| output: false
"""Fetch open-access full texts for the included records of the 2026-10-13 literature review.

For every row of 02.inputs/derived/review-records.csv with decision include and a DOI, asks
OpenAlex for the work's best open-access location and downloads the PDF into
04.references/literature/review/, which is not committed. Writes one row per record to
02.inputs/derived/review-fulltext-log.csv with the route and the outcome, so the count of
records whose full text could not be obtained is measured rather than estimated. Downloaded
files are untrusted data and nothing is executed from that folder. Runs only while the
log does not exist.
"""
import csv, json, os, re, time, urllib.parse, urllib.request

ROOT = os.path.abspath("..")
TABLE = os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "derived", "review-records.csv")
LOG = os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "derived", "review-fulltext-log.csv")
OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "04.references", "literature", "review")
MAILTO = "seamusrobertmurphy@gmail.com"
UA = "forest-fire-index-trends review fetch (mailto:" + MAILTO + ")"

def get_json(url):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        return json.load(r)

def download(url, path):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0", "Accept": "application/pdf"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=90) as r:
        data = r.read()
    if not data.startswith(b"%PDF"):
        return "not a pdf"
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(data)
    return "saved"

def main():
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    with open(TABLE, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(f) if r["decision"] == "include" and r["doi"]]
    done = {}
    if os.path.exists(LOG):
        with open(LOG, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
            done = {r["doi"]: r for r in csv.DictReader(f)}
    log = list(done.values())
    for r in rows:
        if r["doi"] in done and done[r["doi"]]["status"] == "saved":
            continue
        name = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", r["doi"]) + ".pdf"
        path = os.path.join(OUT, name)
        status, url = "", ""
        if os.path.exists(path):
            status = "saved"
        else:
            try:
                # OpenAlex works endpoint, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works
                w = get_json("https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/" + urllib.parse.quote(r["doi"]) + "?mailto=" + MAILTO)
                loc = w.get("best_oa_location") or {}
                url = loc.get("pdf_url") or (w.get("open_access") or {}).get("oa_url") or ""
                if not url:
                    status = "no open copy"
                else:
                    try:
                        status = download(url, path)
                    except Exception as e:
                        status = "download failed " + str(e)[:80]
            except Exception as e:
                status = "openalex failed " + str(e)[:80]
            time.sleep(0.3)
        done[r["doi"]] = {"id": r["id"], "doi": r["doi"], "year": r["year"], "title": r["title"][:120], "url": url, "file": name if status == "saved" else "", "status": status, "date": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")}
    with open(LOG, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["id", "doi", "year", "title", "url", "file", "status", "date"]); w.writeheader(); w.writerows(done.values())
    from collections import Counter
    print(Counter(v["status"][:20] for v in done.values()).most_common())

if not os.path.exists(LOG):
    main()
```
